question.problem:
In a city, $55%$ of the people have blood type O+. Using the normal approximation to the binomial distribution, approximate the probability that if $300$ people are picked at random, then $180$ of them will have blood type O+. Give your answer to three decimal places. *Hint: The data below is taken from the table of values of the cumulative distribution function $Φ(z)$ for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,1.6\,$ $\,0.9452\,$ $\,0.9463\,$ $\,0.9474\,$
$\,1.7\,$ $\,0.9554\,$ $\,0.9564\,$ $\,0.9573\,$
$\,1.8\,$ $\,0.9641\,$ $\,0.9649\,$ $\,0.9656\,$
$z$$\,0.07\,$$\,0.08\,$$\,0.09\,$
$\,1.6\,$ $\,0.9525\,$ $\,0.9535\,$ $\,0.9545\,$
$\,1.7\,$ $\,0.9616\,$ $\,0.9625\,$ $\,0.9633\,$
$\,1.8\,$ $\,0.9693\,$ $\,0.9699\,$ $\,0.9706\,$
question.worked_solution:
Given a binomial random variable $X∼B(n,p),$ if 

- $np>5,$ and

- $n(1-p)>5,$

we can approximate $X$ as a normal random variable $Y$ with mean $\mu =np$ and variance ${\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p),$ that is, 

$$
Y∼N(np,np(1-p)).
$$

Here, we have $n=300$ and $p=0.55.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}np & =300\cdot 0.55 \\  & =165 \\  & >5\,✓ \\ n(1-p) & =300\cdot (1-0.55) \\  & =135 \\  & >5.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can approximate our binomial random variable $X$ with a normal random variable $Y$ with mean

$$
\mu =np=(300)(0.55)=165
$$

and variance

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=np(1-p)=(300)(0.55)(1-0.55)=74.25.
$$

That is, we can approximate $X$ by $Y∼N(165,74.25).$

Now, we can approximate the desired probability $P(X=180).$ Using a continuity correction, we have

$$
P(X=180)≈P(179.5\le Y\le 180.5).
$$

To compute this probability, we transform to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(179.5\le Y\le 180.5) & =P(\frac{179.5-165}{\sqrt{74.25}}\le Z\le \frac{180.5-165}{\sqrt{74.25}}) \\  & ≈P(1.68\le Z\le 1.80) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.80)-P(Z<1.68) \\  & =P(Z\le 1.80)-P(Z\le 1.68) \\  & =Φ(1.80)-Φ(1.68) \\  & =0.9641-0.9535 \\  & =0.0106\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
P(X=180)≈0.011.
$$

Note: Using a software package for the approximation gives a probability of $0.0102.$
